text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 1.8% today after a two-week rally that had pushed the stock up 15.6%. The pullback comes as geopolitical developments—including a reported U.S.-Russia diesel supply deal and talk of potential American military involvement against Iran-backed Houthis in the Red Sea—create uncertainty about global energy supply and refining dynamics. Oil prices remain elevated (U.S. crude at $96/barrel, global at $125), but the conflicting signals about sanctions, supply agreements, and military escalation appear to have taken some wind out of the recent momentum.

Refineries are running at 92.7% capacity with diesel stockpiles at relatively low levels, which had supported the rally. However, if the reported diesel imports from Russia and de-escalation between Russia and Ukraine actually materialize, it could ease the tight supply conditions that have buoyed refining margins in recent weeks—potentially explaining why the stock gave back some gains today despite the fundamental support still being in place.
